AGENTS.md.content:
# Hiroba app agent guide

Use Conventional Commits and independently versioned components. Keep canonical observability in observability/ and regenerate chart/pack outputs with the workflow library. All external actions and reusable workflows use full commit SHAs with version comments. Never add classic Helm indexes, UI Release assets, mutable release callers, or real-environment smoke execution. Use only public Inari SDK contracts.

CONTRIBUTING.md.content:
# Contributing

Open a pull request with Conventional Commits. All applicable workflow lanes must pass, including negative generated-output checks. Do not commit secrets, customer data, generated diagnostics, or registry credentials.

Read the [Hiroba governance](https://github.com/7K-Hiroba/community/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md), [onboarding checklist](https://github.com/7K-Hiroba/community/blob/main/docs/governance/onboarding.md), and [trust-tier policy](https://github.com/7K-Hiroba/community/blob/main/docs/governance/trust-tiers.md). External contributions are currently paused while CLA coverage is reviewed; do not merge an external PR until the organization enables that process. Visit the [Hiroba organization profile](https://github.com/7K-Hiroba) for community context.

README.md.content:
# matrix-app

This is an experimental Hiroba community application repository generated by `inari hiroba init`. It uses the one-repository-per-application layout, independently versioned OCI artifacts, immutable workflow callers, and the public Inari SDK contracts.

## Before onboarding

Reserve the permanent app ID in [`7K-Hiroba/community`](https://github.com/7K-Hiroba/community/blob/main/registry/apps.json), create the owning maintainer team, and complete [application onboarding](https://github.com/7K-Hiroba/community/blob/main/docs/governance/onboarding.md). The generated sources do not claim that a repository, team, release, or trusted source already exists.

After the package is published and its trusted source is configured, deploy it with its canonical source-qualified identity:

~~~sh
inari deploy <source>/matrix-app --cluster <cluster-id> --file values.yaml
~~~

Short package names are local/display names only. Use the canonical `<source>/<package>` form when names collide.

## Development

Keep `package.yaml`/`template.yaml`, values schemas, canonical observability assets, generated chart/pack output, indexes, and release metadata synchronized. Run the repository's immutable PR callers and regeneration checks before submitting changes. Chartless observability still publishes the companion pack; chart-native output is optional. Fixture-only smoke suites are CI-only and are not application evidence.

The optional UI uses the stable `@7k-inari/ui-plugin-sdk@0.1.8` registry release and canonical `inari-ui-ext build`; no clone, postinstall, custom-webpack, or `@7k-hiroba` npm scope is used.

SECURITY.md.content:
# Security

Report vulnerabilities privately to the 7K-Hiroba security maintainers. This scaffold is CI-only and must never be deployed to production. Reviewed artifacts require valid cosign signatures, SLSA provenance, and current signed test evidence.

packages/matrix-app/tests/run.sh.content:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
PACKAGE_DIR=$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)
python3 - "$PACKAGE_DIR" <<'PY'
import json
import sys
from pathlib import Path

import jsonschema
import yaml

package = Path(sys.argv[1])
manifest = yaml.safe_load((package / "package.yaml").read_text())
chart = yaml.safe_load((package / "chart.yaml").read_text())
assert manifest["type"] == "platform-app"
assert chart["repoURL"].startswith("oci://")
assert chart["chart"]
schema = json.loads((package / "values.schema.json").read_text())
jsonschema.validators.validator_for(schema).check_schema(schema)
jsonschema.validate(yaml.safe_load((package / "values-defaults.yaml").read_text()), schema)
print("platform-app manifest and values are valid; no local chart was selected")
PY

tests/smoke/README.md.content:
# Fixture-only runtime smoke

This chartless suite deploys the digest-pinned synthetic HTTP application in `fixtures/app/` and asserts its Service response through Argo Workflows. It uses the explicit `manifests` adapter and contains no application chart, package, or plugin component.

`fixtureOnly: true`, `executableProfiles: [ci]`, `evidenceScope: fixture`, and `appEvidenceEligible: false` are machine-enforced. This suite proves only the synthetic fixture. It cannot satisfy reviewed/official application runtime evidence or real stage/prod application verification. Replace it with an artifact-bound target before making those claims.

Run the local CI journey with the workflow library's `test-runtime-smoke.yml` caller or `run-runtime-smoke.sh --mode local --profile ci`.

tests/smoke/fixtures/app/deployment.yaml.content:
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: matrix-app-fixture
  namespace: default
  labels: {app.kubernetes.io/name: matrix-app-fixture}
spec:
  replicas: 1
  selector:
    matchLabels: {app.kubernetes.io/name: matrix-app-fixture}
  template:
    metadata:
      labels: {app.kubernetes.io/name: matrix-app-fixture}
    spec:
      automountServiceAccountToken: false
      securityContext:
        runAsNonRoot: true
        runAsUser: 101
        seccompProfile: {type: RuntimeDefault}
      containers:
        - name: fixture
          image: nginxinc/nginx-unprivileged@sha256:c38007e929d1d368ea26df1b696bfc5655e274db11f755fad63c25950a157423
          imagePullPolicy: IfNotPresent
          ports: [{name: http, containerPort: 8080}]
          readinessProbe:
            httpGet: {path: /, port: http}
            periodSeconds: 2
            failureThreshold: 15
          securityContext:
            allowPrivilegeEscalation: false
            capabilities: {drop: [ALL]}
          resources:
            requests: {cpu: 25m, memory: 32Mi}
            limits: {cpu: 200m, memory: 128Mi}

tests/smoke/fixtures/app/service.yaml.content:
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: matrix-app-fixture
  namespace: default
spec:
  type: ClusterIP
  selector: {app.kubernetes.io/name: matrix-app-fixture}
  ports:
    - {name: http, port: 8080, targetPort: http}

tests/smoke/suite.yaml.content:
suiteSchema: inari.smoke.v1
target:
  id: matrix-app-smoke
  version: 0.1.0
  adapter:
    kind: manifests
    path: fixtures/app
    fixtureOnly: true
    readiness:
      - {kind: Deployment, name: matrix-app-fixture, namespace: default, condition: Available}
executableProfiles: [ci]
compatibleAppVersions: ">=0.1.0 <2.0.0"
parameterContract: inari.smoke.params.v1
dependencies: []
timeout: 5m
profiles:
  ci: {sideEffects: readOnly, cleanup: required}
  stage: {sideEffects: readOnly, cleanup: required}
  prod: {sideEffects: readOnly, cleanup: required}
rbacRequirements:
  - verbs: [get, list]
    resources: [pods, services]
workflowTemplate: workflowtemplate.yaml
entrypoint: smoke
idempotency: safe
cleanup: no resources are created by the read-only journey

tests/smoke/workflowtemplate.yaml.content:
apiVersion: argoproj.io/v1alpha1
kind: WorkflowTemplate
metadata:
  name: matrix-app-fixture
  namespace: default
  labels:
    inari.dev/smoke-target: matrix-app-smoke
    inari.dev/suite-schema: inari.smoke.v1
spec:
  entrypoint: smoke
  activeDeadlineSeconds: 300
  ttlStrategy:
    secondsAfterCompletion: 300
    secondsAfterFailure: 3600
  templates:
    - name: smoke
      retryStrategy:
        limit: 1
      container:
        name: smoke
        image: curlimages/curl:8.11.1@sha256:9be9b39ac2a66b98bef6d1e1e615af8ff50ec2e746b9163bc12f2bdbf14a949d
        imagePullPolicy: IfNotPresent
        command: [sh, -c]
        args:
          - >-
            curl --fail --silent --show-error --max-time 10 http://matrix-app-fixture.default.svc:8080/ |
            grep -q 'Welcome to nginx'
        securityContext:
          runAsNonRoot: true
          runAsUser: 100
          runAsGroup: 101
          allowPrivilegeEscalation: false
          readOnlyRootFilesystem: true
          capabilities: {drop: [ALL]}
